claim: arch_release.md: 'A tag-triggered GoReleaser build turning a version tag into a GitHub Release... The GoReleaser configuration and the release workflow are the source of truth for how a release is built; this leaf states the contract they must keep.' The ReleasePipeline component (649f5268a2b2) is scoped to an implementer bead, which assumes an implementer box can author and land the release GitHub Actions workflow file the same way it lands any other file in a normal feature-branch PR.
authoritative_source: The push transport itself: portitor is 'the only GitHub credential' holder (docs/enforcement-migration.md line 5) and forwards accepted implementer branches to GitHub upstream. Its GitHub token does not carry the `workflow` OAuth scope, so GitHub itself rejects any push that creates or modifies a file under `.github/workflows/` before it ever reaches a PR — independent of content, signing, or role. Implementer boxes are further restricted to `portitor pr` only ('portitor: only `portitor pr` is allowed'), so there is no self-service recovery (the suggested `portitor reconcile --repo <name>` is not in the implementer's allowed command set).
evidence: Committed .goreleaser.yaml and .github/workflows/release.yml on this branch (signed commit cad4e24) per arch_release.md's build-matrix, trust-chain, and release-assets sections, then `git push`. The push to the internal git server succeeded (branch fast-forwarded), but the upstream forward failed: 'remote: portitor: forward refs/heads/spexmachina-ow43.3 -> upstream FAILED: ... remote rejected ... (refusing to allow a Personal Access Token to create or update workflow `.github/workflows/release.yml` without `workflow` scope)'. No PR was opened as a result. This is structural, not a content-rule rejection (unlike the documented spec/ gate), and it blocks every component in this module whose deliverable includes a workflow file: ReleasePipeline (this bead), and — by the same mechanism — CIPipeline (spexmachina-ow43.2, arch_ci.md) and SpecGate (spexmachina-ow43.1, arch_spec_gate.md) once they reach an implementer.
proposed_fix: Either (a) grant portitor's GitHub-forwarding credential the `workflow` scope (classic PAT) or an equivalent `workflows: write` permission (GitHub App installation token), so implementer branches touching `.github/workflows/*` can land through the normal push-review-merge path like any other file; or (b) if workflow files are meant to stay human-gated for supply-chain reasons (the same posture as spec/), say so explicitly in the delivery module and change CIPipeline/SpecGate/ReleasePipeline's scoping so the workflow YAML is authored in the interactive/authoring loop rather than assigned to an implementer bead — leaving the implementer only the non-workflow artifacts (e.g. .goreleaser.yaml, which pushed without issue).
